MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  OCTOBER 14, 2024
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  5:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Stewart called the meeting to order at 4: 1 5 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Doug Stewart; Mayor Pro Tem Marianne Riggins;  and
  Councilmembers Paul Grisanti, Bruce Silverstein and Steve Uhring.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: None.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

  At 4:16 p.m., the Council recessed to Closed Session to discuss the following items listed
  on the Closed Session agenda:

Conference with Real Property Negotiators Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.8

  Property Known as Malibu Coast Animal Hospital: 23431 Pacific Coast Hwy, APN

  Negotiating Parties: David Marler
  Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment

  2.  Property Known as Super Care: Drugs Pharmacy: 23661 Pacific Coast Hwy, APN
  4458-020-903
  City Negotiator: Assistant City Manager Joe Toney or his Designee.
  Negotiating Patties: Tomas Park
  Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment

Conference with Legal Counsel — Anticipated Litigation

  Initiation of litigation pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (d) of Government
  Code section 54956.9
  Number of potential cases: (2)

  Minutes of October 14, 2024

REGULAR SESSION CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Stewart called the meeting to order at 5:43 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Doug Stewart; Mayor Pro Tem Marianne Riggins; and
  Councilmembers Paul Grisanti, Bruce Silverstein and Steve Uhring.

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Steve McClary, City Manager;
  Joseph Toney, Assistant City Manager; Alexis Brown, Deputy City Manager; Kelsey
  Pettijohn, City Clerk; Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Yolanda Bundy,
  Environmental Sustainability Director; Maureen Tamuri, Interim Planning Director; Susan
  Duenas, Public Safety Director; Rob DuBoux, Public Works Director; Parker Davis, Media
  Technician; Jason Lawrence, Deputy City Clerk; Sarah Flores, Emergency Services
  Coordinator; Jerry Vandermuelen, Fire Safety Liaison; and Bradley Yocum, Fire Safety
  Liaison

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Time Pera led the Pledge ofAllegiance.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Interim City Attomey Rusin reported that the meeting convened at 4:15 p.m., after which
  time the City Council recessed to a Closed Session pursuant to Govemment Code Sections
  54956.9(d)(4) and 54956.8, with all Councilmembers present. He stated the Council
  discussed the items on the Closed Session agenda and took no reportable action.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettijohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on
  October 4, 2024, with the amended agenda posted on October ll, 2024.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Councilmember Grisanti moved, and Mayor Pro Tem Riggins seconded a motion
  to approve the agenda, adjouming in memory of Pete Lippman, Paul Randall, and
  Jo Ruggles. The motion carried unanimously.

ITEM l  CONSENT CALENDAR

  The Mayor opened the floor for public comment on the Consent Calendar. As there
  were no speakers present, he returned the matter to the table for discussion.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of October 14, 2024
  Page 3 of 11

  Item Nos. 1.B.8. was pulled by the Council.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a motion
  to approve the Consent Calendar, pulling Item No. 1.B.8. The motion carried
  unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  l.  Second Reading and Adoption of Ordinance No. 523
  Recommended Action: Conduct second reading, unless waived, and adopt
  Ordinance No. 523 approving Local Coastal Program Amendment No. 20-
  001 and Zone Text Amendment No. 20-002 to update regulations and
  determining the amendments are exempt from the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA).
  New Items
  l.  Waive Further Reading
  Recommended Action: After the City Attomey has read the title, waive full
  reading of ordinances considered on this agenda for introduction on first
  reading and/0r second reading and adoption.
  Approve Warrants
  Recommended Action: Allow and approve warrant demand numbers
  73658-73860 on the register from the General Fund and direct the City
  Manager to pay out the funds to each of the claimants listed in Warrant
  Register No. 755 in the amount of the warrant appearing opposite their
  names, for the purposes stated on the respective demands in a total amount
  of $ 4,370,519.83. City of Malibu payroll check number 5485 and ACH
  deposits were issued in the amount of $785,197.34.
  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the August l9, 2024
  Special meeting and August 26, 2024 Regular meeting.
  Investment Report for the Month Ending August 3 l, 2024
  Recommended Action: Receive the Investment Report for the month
  ending August 31, 2024..
  Beverage Container Recycling_Grant Program
  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 24-53 authorizing the
  submittal of an application for grant funds through the Department of
  Resources Recycling and Recovery (CalRecycle) Beverage Container
  Recycling Grant Program.
  Resolution Declaring the Existence of a Local Emergency and Initiating a
  Program for Reducing the Risk of Fires Associated with Individuals
  Engaged in Unpermitted Camping
  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 24-54 declaring the existence
  of a local emergency and initiating a program for reducing the risk of fires
  associated with individuals engaged in unpermitted camping.
  Approve Amendment to Contract for Special Legal Services with Leech,
  Tishman, Fuscado & Lampl, Inc. to Provide for Representation of the City
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of October 14, 2024
  Page 4 of 11

  related to the Matter of City of Malibu V. Federal Aviation Administration
  related to Aviation Noise and Impacts Generated from Changes to Los
  Angeles International Airport Flight Paths
  Recommended Action: Authorize the City Manager to execute a flfth
  amendment to the Agreement for Legal Services with Leech, Tishman,
  Fuscado & Lampl, Inc. for representation of the City related to the matter
  of Malibu v. Federal Aviation Administration, No. 24-2503.

  The following item was pulled from the consent calendar for individual consideration:

  8.  Assignment of Interest in Malibu Lumber Yard Ground Lease
  Recommended Action:  l) Approve, subject to implementing
  documentation, the transfer of all rights and obligations under the ground
  lease for the Malibu Lumber Yard site dated June 9, 2008 (Ground Lease),
  of WPG Malibu LLC (WPG), the tenant of the Malibu Lumber Yard
  (located at 3939 Cross Creek Road), to AJS Lumberyard, LLC, (AJS) a
  Delaware limited liability company and the execution of a new Guaranty of
  Ground Lease by 9308 Civic Center Drive LLC, a California limited
  liability company; and 2) Authorize the City Manager to execute
  Attachments A-D, and all documents necessary or appropriate to effectuate
  the City’s approval of such changes, in such form as the City Manager shall
  detennine appropriate, with such changes as deemed appropriate by the City
  Manager.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a
  motion to: l) approve, subject to implementing documentation, the transfer
  of all rights and obligations under the ground lease for the Malibu Lumber
  Yard site dated June 9, 2008 (Ground Lease), ofWPG Malibu LLC (WPG),
  the tenant ofthe Malibu Lumber Yard (located at 3939 Cross Creek Road),
  to AJS Lumberyard, LLC, (AJS) a Delaware limited liability company and
  the execution of a new Guaranty of Ground Lease by 9308 Civic Center
  Drive LLC, a California limited liability company; and 2) authorize the City
  Manager to execute Attachments A-D, and all documents necessary or
  appropriate to effectuate the City’s approval of such changes, in such form
  as the City Manager shall determine appropriate, with such changes as
  deemed appropriate by the City Manager. The motion carried 4-1,
  Councilmember Silverstein opposed.

ITEM 2  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  Presentation of Commendation to the Malibu Farmers Market in Recognition of its
  25th Anniversary

  Councilmember Uhring presented the commendation to Debra Bianco.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of October 14, 2024
  Page 5 of 11

  Ms. Bianco thanked the Council and discussed the Cornucopia Foundation’s
  upcoming projects.

  Presentation of Commendation to William Bema for Assisting with a Rescue in
  Malibu Canyon

  Mayor Stewart presented the proclamation Marianne Bema, on behalf of William
  Bema.

  Ms. Bema discussed her son William Bema’s role in the rescue.

  Mr. Bema discussed his brother William Bema’s role in the rescue.

  2024 Fire Season Outlook Presentation

  Public Safety Director Dueflas, Los Angeles County Fire Department Assistant
  Chief Drew Smith, Fire Safety Liaisons Yocum and Vandermuelen, and
  Emergency Services Coordinator Flores presented on fire season outlook and fire
  preparedness programs.

  The Council directed questions to staff and Assistant Chief Smith.

  SB 1297 (Speed Cameras) Implementation Plan Presentation
Lhug

  Deputy City Manager Brown presented on SB 1297 and plans for implementation.

  ITEM 3  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  Jo Drummond, Public Works Commission, discussed the draft traffic study for
  Malibu Canyon Road and plans for safety improvements. She stated there would
  be a community meeting before the projects were presented to the Council. She
  stated the Commission would review the technical design for the Permanent
  Skatepark. She stated the Snack Shack was also going through the design process.

  City Manager McClary stated staff was working on an item regarding the
  Mobilehome Park Rent Stabilization Commission and would begin advertising for
  the vacancies on the Commission. He stated he spoke with State Parks regarding
  the invasive Arundo plant in Malibu Creek and State Parks would address it. He
  announced another Pacific Coast Highway (PCH) Master Plan Feasibility Study
  workshop on October 23, 2024. He announced a candlelight vigil on October l7,
  2024 in honor ofthe Pepperdine students killed in a car crash on October l7, 2023.
  He stated there would also be a media event focusing on PCH safety on October
  18, 2024 at the ghost tires memorial. He announced the City had received the
  Certificate of Achievement for Excellence in Financial Reporting from the
  Govemment Finance Officers Association for the 23rd year in a row. He thanked
  the Finance Division for their work. He stated the City’s draft Housing Element
  had been submitted to HCD. He stated the Regional Water Quality Control Board
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of October 14, 2024
  Page 6 of 11

  would consider an amendment to the MOU with the City regarding the prohibition
  on onsite wastewater treatment facilities in the Civic Center area. He announced a
  Special meeting on October 24, 2024 on the community lands outreach project
  outcomes. He stated he had been contacted by property owners inquiring ifthe City
  would consider purchasing additional property.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back an item on the potential
  purchase of two properties (3542 Coast View Drive and 6551 Portshead Road).

  City Manager McClary announced the October 28, 2024 agenda would include
  items on the Mobilehome Park Rent Stabilization Commission, school district
  separation agreements, FY 2024-25 Strategic Priorities, naming rights for City
  facilities, and the road race agreement. He stated he, Deputy City Manager Brown,
  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins, and Mayor Stewart attended Camp Kilpatrick tour with
  Supervisor Horvath’s office. He stated he planned to attend the League of
  California Cities Annual Conference.

  In response to Councilmember Silverstein and Mayor Pro Tem Riggins, Public
  Works Director DuBoux stated the diagonal parking spaces along the south side
  Civic Center Way were each half in Legacy Park and half in the public right-of-
  way. He stated the parking spaces along the north side were entirely in the public
  right-of-way.

  Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff Department, commended
  William Bema. He reported there were 31 fewer property crimes compared to last
  year. He discussed an incident on October 9, 2024 where a transient at Malibu
  Fitness was threatening staff. He discussed an incident at Topanga Beach where a
  transient assaulted surfer’s car and assaulted the surfer. He discussed a cleanup
  event with Caltrans near Coastline Drive. He discussed a fatal traffic collision near
  Topanga Canyon. He reminded everyone to drive safely. He presented a video on
  the Malibu/Lost Hills Station real time crime center.

  In response to Councilmember Grisanti, Sergeant Soderlund discussed the response
  to an unpermitted car show near Saddle Peak.

ITEM 4.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Ranger Tim Pera, Mountains Recreation Conservation Authority (MRCA),
  presented the monthly ranger report. He stated seven administrative citations were
  issued at Escondido and Lechuza beach for possession of alcohol, smoking, dogs
  on the beach, and illegal off-trail use. He stated 467 parking citations were issued
  at coastal parks. He discussed homeless outreach at Malibu Bluffs and encampment
  cleanup. He stated he had received a report of two new encampments and
  additional outreach efforts were being planned. He stated there were extended f1re
  patrols due to weather events.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of October 14, 2024
  Page 7 of 11

  Howard Ferguson deferred time to Candace Ferguson.

  Candace Ferguson, Point Dume Club Residents Association, requested the Council
  reactivate the Mobilehome Park Rent Stabilization Commission. She suggested
  individuals who could serve as commissioners.

  Rob Blackman requested the Council reactivate the Mobilehome Park Rent
  Stabilization Commission. He discussed the recent sale of the Point Dume Club
  Mobilehome Park.

  Dru Ann Jacobson requested the Council reactivate the Mobilehome Park Rent
  Stabilization Commission.

  Michel Shane discussed the crash that killed the four Pepperdine students. He
  requested the City declare October 17 as Safe PCH Day.

  Larry discussed Bruce Silverstein’s Facebook meme page and described some of
  the memes he found distasteful.

  Aaron discussed the adoption of the 2024 Emergency Operations Plan.

L  J
  Mayor Stewart requested the speaker hold his comments until the agendized item
  is heard.

  Bill Sampson indicated support for Safe PCH Day. He indicated support for
  reactivating the Mobilehome Park Rent Stabilization Commission. He stated he
  was willing to serve on the Commission.

  Andy Lyon addressed Larry’s comments. He announced he was running as a write-
  in candidate for City Council.

  Fred Dora discussed the recent ruling the favor of the City in the litigation between
  MTC and the City. He encouraged the City to collect the legal fees owed as a result
  of the ruling.

  Ann Doneen discussed politics around the General Municipal Election. She
  discussed how the mission of MTC aligned with the City’s Mission Statement. She
  discussed rumors regarding MTC, Councilmember Uhring, John Mazza, and Jo
  Drummond.

  Jo Drummond discussed the comments from Zoom participants regarding
  Councilmember Uhring and Councilmember Silverstein. She objected to the
  statements made regarding her and Councilmember Silverstein. She discussed
  litigation with MTC and the end of the Malibu Bluffs/Charmlee Park swap.

  ITEM 4.B.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of October 14, 2024
  Page 8 of 11

  Councilmember Silverstein indicated support for reactivating the Mobilehome Park
  Rent Stabilization Commission. He suggested the mobilehome park residents
  nominate Commissioners. He indicated support for Safe PCH Day.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staffto consider declaring October 17 Safe PCH
  Day.

  Councilmember Silverstein discussed the new meeting start time and format and
  the efficiencies of the new format. He suggested recognizing Chumash and
  Indigenous People’s Day.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back an item to consider
  recognizing Indigenous People’s Day.

  Councilmember Silverstein discussed the purpose ofthe Facebook meme group and
  the large volume of memes that had been posted.

  Councilmember Uhring discussed comments from the Zoom speakers. He
  discussed the Malibu Times article on Keegan Gibb’s work with the Malibu Fire
  Brigades. He requested a summary ofhow Planning staffwas preparing staff report
  recommendations.

  City Manager McClary confirmed staff would distribute a memo regarding
  Planning staff reports.

  Councilmember Uhring discussed increasing fire insurance costs and the
  challenges for residents to find insurance providers will to provide coverage in
  Malibu.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tem Riggins, Ranger Pera discussed the MRCA’s fire
  division and contractor brush clearance projects.

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins thanked staff for its work on all the major projects. She
  discussed the Camp Kilpatrick tour. She stated she attended the JPIA Risk
  Management Conference. She stated she attended a Public Safety Commission
  meeting and requested the tov’vyard item be scheduled as soon as possible.

  City Manager McClary confirmed staff was working on the tow yard item.

  Councilmember Grisanti stated the Council had held several special meetings in
  recent weeks to move the City’s business forward.

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins announced the Malibu Methodist Pie Festival October l9,
  2024.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of October 14, 2024
  Page 9 of 11

  Mayor Stewart stated he attended an Administration and Finance Subcommittee
  meeting and an ice cream social for City staff. He stated he attended the ribbon
  cutting for the real time crime center at the Malibu/Lost Hills Station. He discussed
  the Camp Kilpatrick tour and how the residents were selected for the Camp
  Kilpatrick program. He stated he attended the business roundtable meeting. He
  stated he attended a remembrance ceremony at Calabasas City Hall for Israel. He
  indicated support for PCH Safety Day. He discussed his support for the Fire
  Brigade program and its purpose. He discussed Mobilehome Park Rent
  Stabilization Commissioner recruitment and appointment. He discussed the home
  insurance issues in Malibu and nationally.

  Councilmember Silverstein discussed the previous plans for Camp Kilpatrick and
  how the facility was being used now.

RECESS  At 8:18 p.m., Mayor Stewart recessed the meeting. The meeting resumed at 8:27
  p.m. with all Councilmembers present.
ITEM 5  ORDINANCES AND PUBLIC HEARINGS

  None.

ITEM 6  OLD BUSINESS

  Strategic Workplan Fiscal Year 24-25
  Recommended Action: Continue this item to the October 28, 2024 Regular City
  Council meeting.

  This item was continued upon approval of the agenda.

ITEM 7  NEW BUSINESS

  Code of Conduct
  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 24-52 establishing a Code of
  Conduct for City Officials.

  Assistant City Manager Toney and Deputy City Manager Brown presented the staff
  report.

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment. As there were no speakers
  present, Mayor Stewart retumed the matter to the table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a motion
  to adopt Resolution No. 24-52 establishing a Code of Conduct for City Officials.
  The motion carried 4-1 , Councilmember Uhring abstained.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of October 14, 2024
  Page 10 of 11

  Adoption of the 2024 Emergency Operations Plan
  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 24-51 adopting the 2024 Emergency
  Operations Plan.

  Emergency Services Coordinator Flores presented the staff report.

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment. As there were no speakers
  present, Mayor Stewart returned the matter to the table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved to adopt Resolution No. 24-51 adopting the
  2024 Emergency Operations Plan.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins seconded the motion.

  The Council discussed the item.

  The motion carried unanimously.

  Appropriation of Office of Traffic Safety gOTS) Grant Funds for Enforcement
  Operations and Public Education Campaign and Agreement for Public Education
  Campaign
  Recommended Action: Continue this item to the October 28, 2024 Regular City
  Council meeting.

  This item was continued upon approval of the agenda.

ITEM 8  COUNCIL ITEMS

  None.

ADJOURNMENT

  Mayor Stewart adjourned the meeting at 9:32 p.m. in memory of Jo Ruggles, Paul Randall,
  and Pete Lippman.
